root_cause: The public language switcher and static localized-route builder treated both locales as prefixed. That made English to Dutch navigate to /nl/* and caused Dutch canonical, hreflang and internal-link generation to diverge from the agreed public authority where Dutch is unprefixed and English lives under /en/*.
prevention: Dutch public routes are always canonical and unprefixed.
English public routes are always canonical under /en/*.
Runtime language switching must preserve path, query and hash while mapping NL→EN to /en/* and EN→NL to the unprefixed route.
Static localized-route generation must use the same canonical mapping for internal links, canonical URLs, hreflang and og:url.
Legacy /nl and /nl/* URLs permanently redirect to the matching unprefixed Dutch route.
Production browser proof must execute a real NL→EN→NL roundtrip and fail if the Dutch return path contains /nl.

Regression tests that encode superseded operational constants or superseded safety policy must be updated in the same lineage when the canonical implementation changes; stale tests may not force rollback to unsafe behavior.

promotion.purpose: Canonical Production Source Snapshot promotion and NL→EN→NL production proof.
observed_regressions: Two stale route retry tests still asserted attempts=3 after the bounded production verifier moved to attempts=2.
One stale i18n test still asserted production provider failure should degrade to runtime fallback, contradicting the restored fail-closed invariant.
promotion.recovery: Aligned stale regression tests with the current canonical contracts; no weakening of runtime or production proof.

evidence.observed_defect: Public English-to-Dutch switching and static Dutch locale metadata could resolve to /nl/* even though Dutch public canonical authority is unprefixed.
evidence.terminal_requirement: Netlify production must be ready on the protected promotion main SHA and the browser canary must prove NL→EN→NL without any /nl/* Dutch route.
